final_proof:
Let \(X\) be a set and let \(\Sigma\) be a \(\sigma\)-algebra on \(X\). Recall that a magma of sets (with relative set difference as its binary operation) is a nonempty family \(\mathcal M\subseteq\mathcal P(X)\) such that \(E,F\in\mathcal M\) implies \(E\setminus F\in\mathcal M\).

By the axioms of a \(\sigma\)-algebra, \(X\in\Sigma\), so \(\Sigma\) is nonempty. Also \(\varnothing=X^{\mathsf c}\in\Sigma\).

We first show that \(\Sigma\) is closed under binary unions. If \(E,F\in\Sigma\), set
\[
E_1=E,\qquad E_2=F,\qquad E_n=\varnothing\quad(n\ge 3).
\]
Every \(E_n\) belongs to \(\Sigma\), and closure under countable unions gives
\[
E\cup F=\bigcup_{n=1}^{\infty}E_n\in\Sigma.
\]
Complement closure and De Morgan's law then imply closure under binary intersections:
\[
E\cap F=(E^{\mathsf c}\cup F^{\mathsf c})^{\mathsf c}\in\Sigma.
\]

Now let \(A,B\in\Sigma\). Since \(B^{\mathsf c}\in\Sigma\), intersection closure yields
\[
A\setminus B=A\cap B^{\mathsf c}\in\Sigma.
\]
Thus relative set difference is a binary operation on the nonempty family \(\Sigma\). Hence \(\Sigma\) is a magma of sets. (If “magma of sets” is formulated using union as its operation, the binary-union argument above proves the assertion directly.)
